title: Reachable input pairs along a subprotocol path form a rectangle
statement:
Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over Alice's input type $X$ and Bob's input type $Y$, and let $\pi$ be a subprotocol path witnessing that $s$ is a rooted subtree of $p$. Then the set of input pairs
\[
\{(x, y) \in X \times Y : (x,y) \text{ reaches } s \text{ along } \pi\}
\]
is a rectangle. Explicitly, it factors as $A \times B$, where $A \subseteq X$ is the set of Alice inputs consistent with every one of Alice's branching choices along $\pi$ and $B \subseteq Y$ is the set of Bob inputs consistent with every one of Bob's branching choices along $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: a subprotocol path from s to p is given
replaced:
Given a subprotocol path $\texttt{hsp} : \texttt{SubprotocolPath}\,s\,p$, the set of input
pairs $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ that reach $s$ along that path is a combinatorial rectangle
$\texttt{reachXPath}(\texttt{hsp}) \times \texttt{reachYPath}(\texttt{hsp})$.
